title: Google Quantum AI & DeepMind Demonstrate Modular Hyperbolic Codes for Over 30x QEC Overhead Reduction - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Google Quantum AI, DeepMind and MIT proposed modular hyperbolic QEC codes networking small planar chips of about 100 qubits, claiming over 30x lower physical qubit overhead than 2D surface codes in simulation.

insights.claim: An arXiv manuscript from Google Quantum AI, Google DeepMind and MIT shows that networking flat chips of about 100 qubits through static boundary couplers in hyperbolic tiling unlocks qLDPC-like encoding rates without on-chip long-range wire crossings, cutting qubit overhead by more than 30x versus 2D surface codes.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A modular route to high-rate codes could ease hardware requirements for fault tolerance.

insights.claim: The modular hyperbolic color code [[6400,104,30]] needs about 36 physical qubits per logical qubit, versus over 1,000 for a Euclidean surface code, about 48 for the two-gross bivariate bicycle code and about 95 for the modular hyperbolic surface code.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: Simulations with the SI1000 noise model (p=0.1%), decoded with AlphaQubit and correlated MWPM, showed low logical error rates even when inter-module seam noise was 1%, 10x higher than on-chip gate errors.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Tolerance of noisy inter-chip links makes modular networking more realistic; simulation only.

insights.claim: The team developed fault-tolerant walking circuits executing logical gates via code automorphisms, plus modular ribbon extractors about 4.5x smaller than the memory itself.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Addresses logic operations without space overhead.
